principles.title: Agents write the code. I own the decisions.
principles.proof: An agent studies the ticket, records it in a knowledge wiki, and drafts a plan that I and a fresh agent review. The executor agent proves each change with tests it runs locally, such as characterization tests before a refactor. The merge request stays a draft until the reviewer agent and I have both checked it.

stat.label: reviews on every plan and every change

steps.label: open the MR, update the wiki

principles.title: Pin down the old behavior before replacing it.
principles.proof: Captured CheckProof's legacy scheduler in characterization tests, then moved customers' live schedules to the new system with a rollback switch that worked at any point.

principles.title: Make code safe to change, then change it.
principles.proof: Upgraded Luce's Rails monolith from 7.0 to 7.2 by resolving transaction rollback, encryption, and dependency issues, with RSpec and VCR tests as the safety net.

principles.title: Code is cheap now. Proof isn't.
principles.proof: Load-tested CheckProof's task lifecycle monitor against a 1M-task backlog before trusting it: zero failures or deadlocks, and 75% fewer database calls per status change.
